messages:
Mike H: Heads-up — after PR #4123 (int8 asymmetric + kv prefetch stride=4) we're seeing a 12-18% throughput regression on 8xA100 TP configs. Noticed during nightly perf smoke.
Anya L: ugh. regression where exactly? end-to-end latency or tokens/sec drop?
Mike H: Tokens/sec drop across medium-length sequences (512). End-to-end p95 up ~15%. Traces show long all-reduce stalls between TP stages.
Sophia R: Can you paste the profiler snapshot?
Mike H: Sure — quick flame output from perf-agent on one failing run:
```
PROFILE SUMMARY:
kernel_compute: 62.3ms
allreduce_wait: 41.2ms
kv_prefetch_wait: 18.5ms
swap_kv: 5.8ms
other: 3.4ms
TOTAL_STEP: 131.2ms
```
Mike H: Allreduce wait jumped compared to baseline (was ~18ms).
Raj P: Did the PR change tensor layouts or slice boundaries for TP? That can blow up NCCL overlap and increase comms.
Mike H: PR touched quant scale paths (per-tensor asymmetric int8), and added kv prefetch stride heuristic (prefetch 4 keys ahead to reduce cache misses). No explicit layout changes.
Lee T: The prefetch stride could increase concurrency/pressure on the network if it issues large async fetches across ranks — maybe ends up serialized with allreduce windows.
Anya L: Any sign of precision-related stalls? int8 path adds extra rescale kernels which might run on the critical path and affect overlap.
Mike H: We saw two odd things together: (1) the int8 rescale kernel has non-negligible runtime at seq len=512 (~3.2ms per layer) and (2) kv prefetch issues more RPCs that sometimes land during reduce windows. Combination seems to push allreduce into non-overlapped region.
Sophia R: Example microtrace from layer 18 (timestamps local):
```
L18: compute_attn_forward start -> 0ms
L18: launch_rescale_int8 -> 2.9ms
L18: issue_kv_prefetch(rank+1) -> 3.1ms
L18: allreduce_start -> 6.2ms
allreduce_wait -> 41.0ms
compute_resume -> 47.2ms
```
Sophia R: So rescale + prefetch now precede the allreduce whereas previously they were after or overlapped.
Raj P: That ordering change would definitely ruin comm/compute overlap. Why did ordering shift? kernel selection scheduling?
Lee T: Kernel scheduler picks rescale kernel because int8 path flagged it mandatory before packing tensors for NCCL. Prefetch is launched as soon as KV keys are scheduled; the new stride increased prefetches per layer.
Anya L: Quick hypothesis: prefetch RPCs are pinned to same CUDA stream used by NCCL ops -> forces stream sync -> allreduce can't overlap. We should check streams.
Mike H: Confirmed — current prefetch uses stream 0 for CUDA memhandles. Baseline used a dedicated async stream. PR inadvertently reverted to default.
Sophia R: Okay that's actionable. Two mitigations: revert prefetch to dedicated stream and add a stream-unsafe assert in debug builds; and reduce prefetch stride back to 1 or 2 for TP configs.
Raj P: For int8 rescale kernel: can we fuse the rescale into earlier GEMM kernel or move it to a separate stream that also doesn't block NCCL? Need to be careful with correctness for asymmetric quant.
Anya L: Fusing is ideal but risky short-term. Moving rescale to a non-blocking stream might work if we ensure dependency via CUDA events and that NCCL uses the default stream semantics we expect.
Mike H: I'm going to open a quick revert PR to put prefetch back on async stream and set stride=1 for TP configs, run the nightly. If that recovers perf we can then schedule a follow-up for rescale fusion.
perf-bot: nightly-run 2087-03-14-01 completed — throughput delta for branch: -1.9% compared to baseline (after revert), p95 latency delta: +0.8%.
Mike H: Nice, revert looks promising. Still some small reg, likely due to rescale kernel cost.
Lee T: For the rescale: try a micro-optimization — use vectorized casts (uint8->float32) and precompute scale multipliers in shared memory; also add kernel hint to prefer TensorCores where possible.
Sophia R: Also add a perf testcase that runs TP 8x with seq len 512 and assert tokens/sec >= baseline * 0.98 to prevent regressions.
Anya L: I'll add a CI perf check and a debug-only stream-safety checker.
Mike H: Thanks. I'll land the prefetch revert PR and create an issue to track rescale fusion/faster kernel. Assign to Raj/Lee for kernel work.
Raj P: Sounds good. Can we add logging in perf traces to record stream ids for network ops so next time it's easier to root-cause?
Mike H: Yep will add that to perf-agent.
Sophia R: Sweet. Great teamwork. :thumbsup:
